Guidelines on good clinical laboratory practices 
635. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
 SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI: 
Will the Minister of  HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 

224 
(a) whether ICMR has recently prepared guidelines on Good Clinical 
Laboratory Practices for laboratories engaged, in medical research as 
well as those catering to patient care; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether a large number of laboratories engaged in medical research 
are not providing right reports resulting in wrong treatment of patients; 
and 
(d) if so, the manner in which such a control would be exercised by 
Government on such diagnostic and pathological laboratories? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. ICMR has recently 
prepared Guidelines on Good Clinical Laboratory Practices (GCLP) for 
laboratories engaged in medical research as well as those catering to 
patient care. Generation of laboratory results is a teamwork involving 
patient preparation, collection of sample and its processing, analysis, 
reporting of results and its transmission to the researcher/treating 
doctor and patient. To minimize errors, laboratories should follow laid 
down procedures at all times. GCLP guidelines elucidate these stepwise 
procedures which can be adopted by laboratories engaged in research as 
well as patient care. The guidelines can be accessed from ICMR website 
www.icmr.nic.in 
(c) and (d) There is no data on number of laboratories engaged in 
medical research which are not providing right reports resulting in wrong 
treatment of patients in India. However, published reports indicate the 
need for taking measures for detecting and preventing errors in 
laboratories. These include laying down rules and responsibilities and 
following them, conducting internal quality control procedures and 
external quality assurance programmes. 
In India, laboratories can volunteer for accreditation of one or more 
services offered by them. The National Accreditation Board for Testing 
and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) has been providing accreditations 
services to medical laboratories since 1998 and is currently following 
ISO 15189; 2007 standards. 
Opening of new medical colleges 
636. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has decided to relax the rules for opening new 
medical colleges in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 

225 
(c) the present status of proposals for new medical colleges pending 
for clearance with Government; and 
(d) the steps taken by Government to clear the pending proposals? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (d) The Government has conveyed its 
decision to the Medical Council  of  India  (MCI)  to  revise  the  norms 
prescribed for opening of new medical colleges in MCI  

226 
Regulations on Minimum Standard Requirement for Medical colleges for 
50/100/150 MBBS Admission Annually. Relaxations have been given in the 
norms for land requirement criteria for campus, bed strength, indoor 
occupancy for opening of medical colleges in the States where National 
Rural Health Mission is operational, North Eastern States, Hill S tates 
and Hilly districts in other States. For opening of new Medical Colleges 
in these areas the total land requirement will be 20 acres in not more 
than two pieces of land separated by a distance of 15 k.m. as against 25 
acres prescribed for other parts of the country. The land separated by a 
road or canal connected with a bridge shall be treated as one piece of 
land for opening of Medical Colleges. The criteria relating to bed 
strength in the teaching hospitals at the time of starting Medical 
College has been revised to 250 beds as against the 300 beds prescribe 
for other parts of the country. The criteria for indoor bed occupancy in 
these areas has been revised to 60%. This will help in opening of new 
medical colleges in unserved and under- served areas of the country and 
also increase the number of medical colleges as well as production of 
doctors in the country. The Ministry has sent 68 proposals for 
establishment of new medical colleges during the year 2009- 10, for their 
technical evaluation and recommendation as per the provisions of the 
Medical Council of India (MCI) Regulations. As per the time schedule 
prescribed in the MCI regulations the last date for grant of permission 
by Central Government is 115th July of each year. 
Mental healthcare facilities 
637. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of  HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether 7 per cent Indians or around 7 crore people in the country 
suffer from mental disorder in one or the other form, but the healthcare 
facilities are woefully inadequate; 
(b) whether the National Human Rights Commission has taken up this 
serious issue with the Medical Council of India; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) what is the action plan of Government to address this concern? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) According to a recent survey conducted 
by the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), 
the prevalence of mental disorders in the country is about 7% of the 
population. Close to 3% of the population need active treatment. Unlike 
in the past, effective medications have reduced the need for admission 

227 
and facilitating patients to get back to their normal schedule first. 
Apart from 43 Govt. Mental Health Institutes, Psychiatric Wings of all 
Medical Colleges and General Hospitals provide treatment facilities for 
mentally ill patients. 
There is, however, shortage of psychiatrists and mental health 
professionals in the country. 
(b) and (c) Following the discussion held under the auspices of the 
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) that Medical Council of India 
(MCI) would create more awareness among medical colleges to take up 
Postgraduate course in Psychiatry to cover the shortage of manpower in 
the  field, the NHRC had asked the MCI to indicate the steps being taken 
by it to increase the number  

228 
of Psychiatrists in the country. The MCI has reported that it has already 
granted permission during the years 2005 to 2008 for starting MD 
(Psychiatry) degree course to 18 institutes, DPM course to 7 institutes 
and increasing the number of seats in MD (Psychiatry) course to 4 
Institutes. This has resulted in addition of 25 seats in MD (Psychiatry) 
course and 8 seats in DPM course. 
(d) Under National Mental Health Programme, efforts are made to 
provide mental health services as a part of general health system. In 
this regard, Central Government supplements the State Governments' 
efforts through District Mental health Programme (DMHP), upgradation of 
Psychiatric Wings of Medical Colleges/General Hospitals and 
strengthening/modernisation of Mental hospitals to make them as 
therapeutic units. The Central Government has proposed to restrategise  
the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) during the 11th five Year 
Plan to extend DMHP to more districts in the country in a phased manner. 
To address the acute shortage of qualified mental health professionals in 
the country, manpower development schemes under the NMHP for setting up 
of centres of excellence in mental health and PG training departments in 
mental health specialities are under active consideration. Training is 
also being provided to medical officers and health staff to implement the 
Programme. It has been proposed to intensify training using standard 
training modules both in terms of duration and frequency. 
Progress made to control MMR and IMR by NRHM 
638. SHRI B. J. PANDA: 
 MS. MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to set up new medical facilities in under-
developed States i.e. Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Jharkhand etc. under the 
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM); 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) what is the progress that has so far been made to control MMR/IMR 
in Orissa, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh etc. under this Mission; 
(d) what is the status of allocation of funds under this project to 
Orissa and Jharkhand States during 2008-09 fiscal; 
(e) whether Orissa and Jhark hand States have made certain additional 
demands towards development of infrastructure facilities to improve their 
health card among the States; and 

229 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) Government of India has launched 
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) in 2005 to provide accessible, 
affordable and quality health care to rural population, especially to the 
vulnerable section wherein financial assistance is given to the 
States/UTs for construction/maintenance/upgradation of rural Health 
Infrastructure in the States including Madhya Pradesh, Orissa and 
Jharkhand. Government of India bears the entire capital expenditure for 
construction/re-design  of  building  in a phased manner over the mission 
period for construction and  

230 
upgradation of Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Community Health Centres 
(CHCs). Besides this, assistance is provided to the States/U.Ts in the 
form of Untied Grants, Annual Maintenance Grants, Grants to Rogi Kalyan 
Samities/ Hospital Management Committees. 
The upgradation of Rural Health Infrastructure i.e., Sub Centres 
(SCs), Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Community Health Centres (CHCs) 
is an ongoing process and depends on the priority of States, as reflected 
in their annual Programme Implementation Plan under NRHM. A S tatement 
showing functioning of SC, PHCs and CHCs getting funding support under 
NRHM is are enclosed (See below). 
(c) NRHM also includes the second phase of Reproductive and Child 
Health (RCH) Programme, which has been launched with effect from 1.4.2005 
for a period of five years. The Programme aims to reduce Total Fertility 
Rate (TFR), Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) and Maternal Mortality Ratio 
(MMR) in the country. Under the Programme, flexibility is provided to the 
States to devise need based Programme implementation plan amongst other 
(i) address the unmet need for contraception; ii) promote skilled care at 
birth; (iii) increase coverage of immunization; (iv) introduce integrated 
Management of Neonatal and childhood Illness (v) enhance availability of 
facilities for institutional deliveries and emergency obstetric care; 
(vi) provide skilled care to pregnant women at the community level; (vii) 
improve coverage ante-natal and postnatal care and (viii) address other 
related reproductive, maternal and child health care needs of their 
respective populace. 
(d) to (f) Under the NRHM, an amount of Rs.34397.70 lakhs and 
Rs.27837.83 lakhs has been allocated to the States of Orissa and 
Jharkhand respectively during the financial year 2008- 09. The Government 
of India allocates flexible budgetary envelopes to the States and the 
Union Territories and the National Programme Coordination Committee 
approves the annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) of the States 
and the Union Territories. The PIP contains plan of the State for 
development of infrastructure facilities also. Hence, the budgetary 
allocation for development of infrastructure facilities is included in 
the overall annual flexible pool allocation. The States of Orissa and 
Jharkhand has not sought additional budget over and above the flexible 
pool allocation for development of infrastructure facilities.

Closure of vaccine units 
639. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be 
pleased to state: 

233 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had closed down its three 
public sector vaccine units and if so, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that Government has now decided to 
restart the production of vaccine in these units and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(c) on what grounds the earlier closure order has been revoked? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALT H AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) The Government has not taken any 
decision to close down the three Public Sector Vaccine Manufacturing 
Units, namely, the Central Research Institute, Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, 
the Pasteur Institute of India, Coonoor, Tamil Nadu and BCG Vaccine 
Laboratory, Chennai, Tamilnadu. The manufacturing licenses of these three 
Institutes were suspended by the Drugs Controller General of India 
(DCG(I)) in January, 2008 since they were not found in compliance with 
the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as provided under Schedule M of 
Drugs and Cosmetic Rules, 1945. 
(b) and (c) A proposal for upgradation of the facilities at CRI 
Kasauli to make them GMP compliant has now been received WHO experts have 
examined this and have opined that this is feasible. The production of 
vaccines can be restarted after compliance with GMP requirements. 
Shortage of post graduate seats 
640. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the Minister of  HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a huge shortage of Post 
Graduate seats for medical graduates in our country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith the actual number of seats of 
Post Graduates and Medical Graduates at present; and 
(c) by when the P.G. seats are likely to be increased? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (c) At present approximately 11,600 
seats are available in different postgraduate courses for approximately 
23000 MBBS students passed out from various medical colleges across the 
country. Further National Board of Examination also provides nearly 5006 
seats in various DNB courses annually. Thus, Post graduation facilities 
are available for nearly 70% of the MBBS students passing out throughout 
the country. 
As per the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, as amended and the 
Regulations made thereunder, it is for the State Government to decide the 
need to start/increase Post Graduate (P.G.) seats in a medical college. 
The Central Government is giving permission for starting/increase of PG 
seats in a medical college based on the Essentiality Certificate given by 
the respective State Government and availability of infrastructural 

234 
facilities.

Redefining of counterfeit drugs 
645. PROF. ALKA BALRAM KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of  HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether his attention has been drawn to WHO attempt on redefining 
counterfeit drugs and state the initiative taken by Government to 
redefine/counter resolution the definition of counterfeit drugs amongst 
the developing countries; 
(b) whether Government is aware about the private funding by 
international Federation of Pharmaceuticals Manufacturers Associations 
(IFPMA) of multinational pharma companies in International Medical 
Products Anti-counterfeiting Task Force (IMPACT) organization, which is 
pushing for change of definition of counterfeit drugs through WHO; and 
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government to protect the interest of 
poor patients of the developing countries? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) Yes Sir. The Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare had raised its concern in the international meetings of 
WHO on redefining counterfeit drugs. In the meeting of SEARO under WHO in 
September, 2008, India raised objection to the proposed definition of 
Counterfeit medicines as given by IMPACT and an alternative definition 
was proposed in consultation with other developing countries. Matter was 
further taken up in the WHO Executive Board Meeting at Geneva in January, 
2009. As a result of continuous effort of Indian Government & other 
developing countries, the Executive Board of World Health Organizations 
(WHO) requested Director General, WHO to prepare another evidence based 
report outlining in detail the issues relating to "counterfeit" medical 
products in the context of public health. 

260 
(b) Yes Sir. 
(c) Meetings were held with the various pharmaceutical industry 
organizations like Federation of Indian Pharma Entrepreneurs (FOPE), 
Indian Drugs Manufacturers Association (IDMA), Organization of 
Pharmaceutical Producers of India (OPPI), Confederation of India 
Pharmaceuticals Industries  (C1PI),  India  Pharmaceuticals  Alliance  
(IPA),  SME  Pharma  Industries   Confederation  

261 
(SPIC), Third World Network and Pharmaxil to discuss the proposed 
definition on counterfeit medicines. Discussions were held on each and 
every word of the definition of counterfeit medicine as it would affect 
the Indian Generic Industry which caters to the poor patient of India and 
other developing countries. Government is making efforts at every 
international forum to protect the interest of poor patients of the 
developing countries.

Compensation to victims of clinical trials 
647. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in view of growing number of clinical researches in the 
country and also in view of India becoming popular destination for 
clinical research, Government plans to formulate guidelines or code on 
clinical research with emphasis on giving compensation to participants 
who suffer economical, social, psychological and physical damages; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) Guidelines and requirements for 
conducting clinical trial in the country are specified in the Schedule Y 
of Drugs and Cosmetic Rules. 
Clinical Trial in country is required to be conducted as per Schedule 
Y, which also mandates conformance to Indian Good Clinical Practices 
(GCP) Guidelines. The Para 2.4.7 of Indian GCP guidelines prescribes  
provision for compensation to trial subject by sponsor in case of any 
harm caused to them during the trials. 
In order to ensure that Clinical trials are conducted in the country 
as per regulation & Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines, it has been 

266 
felt necessary to register the Organizations conducting clinical trial. 
Draft guidelines for the same have been prepared, which would be placed 
before forthcoming Drugs Technical Advisory Board Meeting to be held on 
23.02.2009. 

267

Sector Banks have taken several measures for providing a stimulus to the

remainder of the financial year.

export credit to SME sector up to 31.03.2009.

Guarantee Scheme reduced from 24 months to 18 months.

2000 crore to the MSME Refinance Fund with SIDBI.

borrowers, banks have been advised to fix separate sub- limits, 
within the overall limits, specifically for meeting payment 
obligations in respect of purchases from MSEs. 
(3) Measures announced by the Public Sector Banks 
 • Public Sector Banks to grant need- based ad hoc Working Capital 
Demand Loans upto 20 per cent of the existing funds based limits 
in respect of units having overall fund based credit facility upto 
Rs. 10 crore. 
 • Reduction in interest rates for borrowing by micro enterprises by 
1 per cent and in respect of SMEs by 0.5 per cent.

MSMEs where project implementation has been delayed in the current 
scenario.

†666. SHRI MOTI LAL VORA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Railways have added one additional berth 
between the two berths adjoining window in three thousand second class 
sleeper compartments, causing a lot of inconvenience to the passengers; 
(b) whether Railways had conducted any survey to know the public 
opinion in this regard; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that 97 per cent of people in South-West 
Zone objected this; and 
(d) the expenditure incurred so far in adding one additional berth in 
between the two berths in the second class sleeper? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): (a) 
In order to enhance the passenger carrying capacity, additional 
longitudinal middle berths were thought to be provided in sleeper class 
coaches. Up to 31.01.2009, about 5190 sleeper class coaches have been 
provided with such berths. 
There have been some passenger complaints about inconvenience and 
discomfort caused by increased congestion and inadequate space in such 
coaches. It has now been decided to discontinue the scheme. 
(b) Yes, Sir. 
(e) During the survey conducted on South Western Railway, 91% of the 
people objected to the introduction of additional side berths in coaches. 
(d) The work of provision of longitudinal middle berths has been 
carried out in various Zonal Railways through the process of tendering. A 
concrete assessment of the expenditure incurred is not available at this 
juncture. However, the average cost of the work is about Rs. 1.3 lakhs 
per sleeper class coach.

†676. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state:

in number of berths from 72 to 81 in reserve coaches, passengers are 
facing great inconvenience;

inconvenience caused due to this increase; 
(c) whether any complaint has been received by Government in this 
regard or Government is aware of the public discontentment; and 
(d) if so, the measures through which Government is considering to 
solve this serious problem?

the Sleeper coaches mainly were of inconvenience and discomfort caused by 
increased congestion and inadequate space.

discontinue the scheme of provision of additional side middle berths in 
sleeper class coaches. Such berths provided in the already modified 
coaches shall be gradually removed within a period of six months.

 SHRI DARA SINGH:

to (c) Railway Protection Force, an Armed Force of the Union under 
Ministry of Railways, is presently supplementing the efforts of the 
respective State Governments in combating terrorist, naxalites and other 
disruptive activities over Railways. Although the maintenance of the law 
and order and to tackle the problem of terrorists, naxalites attacks and 
other disruptive activities over Railways is the responsibility of the 
State Government concerned through Government Railway Police. However, 
Railway Protection Force is supplementing the Government Railway Police 
to tackle such problems. Following measures have been initiated for 
strengthening of RPF viz.- 
i) RPF/RPSF staff have been deployed at important stations and in trains 
and briefed to be prepared to tackle any situation. 
ii) Staffs have been put on alert to prevent such incidents. 
iii) Government Railway Police and State Police have also been asked to 
strengthen the security arrangements at Railway stations and in 

335 
trains. 
iv) Close coordination with State Police and Intelligence agencies 
have been maintained to share information of such acts.

equipment for RPF. 
vi) Allocation of Rs 14.26 Crore for procurement of vehicles for RPF. 

336 
vii) Implementation of an Integrated Security System over all the 
railway stations of four metro cities viz. Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata & 
Chennai and 140 other sensitive/vulnerable railway stations of the 
country. The above system consists of following four broad areas- 
1) IP based CCTV surveillance system. 
2) Access Control 
3) Personal and Baggage Screening System and 
4) Bomb Detection and Disposal System 
viii) RPF has been upgraded with modern weaponry/security gadgets like 
INSAS 5.56mm rifles, AK- 47, SLR 7.62mm, Carbine 9 mm, Pistol 9mm, 
Bullet Proof Jackets and Helmets, Walkie- Talkie, Hand Held Metal 
Detectors, Door Frame Metal Detectors, etc. 
(ix) It has been proposed to give commando training to 2 RPSF Battalions 
and deployment of trained staff at strategic locations. It has also 
been proposed to raise three additional Battalions of RPSF. 
(d) There is no separate Head for Security purposes. Funds are made 
available for the procurement of Security equipments and 
modernization/strengthening of the Railway Protection Force from 
appropriate heads of account like Works Programme, Machinery & Plants 
(M&P) Head, Passenger Amenity Head etc. Allocation of funds for Security 
purposes is made as per requirement.

Extra berths in coaches 
702. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government has decided to drop and reverse the proposal to 
add extra berths in the AC- 3 tier and sleeper class in long distance 
trains in view of complaints of inconvenience from the passengers 
concerned; 
(b) if so, the loss incurred by the Railways in the process of 
creating and dismantling of the added seats and in which trains and how 
many additional berths/seats would have to be dismantled; and 
(c) the alternate steps contemplated to achieve the objective of 
shortening the waiting list and to cut down refunds? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): (a) 
and (b) Yes, Sir. The policy has been reviewed and it has now been 
decided to discontinue the scheme of provision of additional side middle 
berths in sleeper and AC 3 Tier coaches. Such berths, wherever provided 
in the coaches, shall be gradually removed within a period of six months. 
In the mean time, such coaches will be utilized in trains where the 

349 
journey may not involve more than one night. 
The scheme was introduced about 1.5 years back and such coaches have 
been progressively inducted in train services since then, thereby 
providing more reserved accommodation to passengers and, though a 
subsidiary benefit, leading to enhanced earnings as well. The removal of 
such berths shall also be done gradually and therefore, marginal losses, 
that may happen, can not be estimated at this stage. An estimated 52030 
side middle berths shall be required to be dismantled.

Mill Workers' agitation at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi 
SHRI BHARATKUMAR RAUT (Maharashtra): Hon. Deputy Chairman, Sir, I wish 
to attract the attention of the House to the fact that hundreds of mill 
workers and their families have come to Delhi today to stage an 
agitation. Sir, it is an unfortunate thing that the mill workers, who 
were at one time the backbone of Indian economy, have to come all the way 
from Mumbai to Delhi to seek justice. Mumbai came on the map of the world 
economy because of its mills. For 150 years, mills in Mumbai had been 
doing a lot of job for Indian economy. More than that, the mill workers 
in Mumbai were the forerunners and torch- bearers of Indian Independence 
struggle. If you remember, from 1930 onwards, mill workers had been doing 
strikes and agitations for the freedom struggle. What is their plight 
now? At one time, Mumbai has as many as sixty plus textile mills. Today, 
they are not even handful. This is because of the conspiracy between the 
mill-owners, the State Government and some labour union leaders. 
Now, mills have been closed down and that ample land, prime land, 
acres of land has gone to commercial malls, commercial establishments, 
sky scrappers for the rich residents and also discotheques and bowling 
clubs. In such a situation, what happens to the workers who were working 
in the mills and what happens to the residents who were living for ages, 
for generations on the land of mills? Those residents have been forcibly 
evacuated from their houses for some technical reasons. Now, the demand 
of the workers, who have come here, is that they should be given 
legitimate housing on the land which has now been occupied by private 
builders. The Government had agreed to their demand time and again, but 
it is not done. I would request you to use your good office to force the 
Textile Minister to see that this should be done forthwith. Another 
demand of the mill workers of those mills which were closed down, is 
that, at least, one member of the family should be accommodated in the 
industry or the enterprise which comes up on the mill land. I think, it 
is our duty, as the Members of this august House, to protect the 
interests of the workers. With these words, I conclude.

DR. JANARDHAN WAGHMARE (Maharashtra): Thank you, Sir, for giving me 
this opportunity. The Railway Budget that has been presented in the House 
is an Interim Budget. But, the Ministry of Railways has done a 
commendable work and Lalu Prasadji and his colleagues deserve our 
congratulations. The Railway Minister has kept the common man in the 
centre of the affairs of Railways, and facilities are given to the common 
man. Sir, Railways come under public sector, but public sector also can 
be profitable if it is managed professionally and this Department has 
managed its affairs very professionally. That is why they have given us 
profits. In the last five years, they have earned a surplus of Rs. 90,000 
crores. This is indeed a very good performance. Sir, Railways play a very 
important role in the development of the country. It has linked different 
far-flung regions. It has also contributed its mite to the national 
integration also. But, Sir, our country is very big and there are many 
regions where we don't have railway lines. For this, I would like to give 
certain suggestions. Those suggestions could be taken into consideration. 
My first suggestion would be, a master plan to cover the entire country 
should be prepared. The second suggestion, there should be uni- gauge 
throughout the country, that is, broad gauge. Small gauge and medium 
gauge railway lines should be converted into broad gauge railway lines so 
that the whole country can be knit together. The third suggestion is, 
backward regions should be given priority for new railway lines. The 
fourth suggestion is, profits that we get from Railways should be 
utilised for gauge conversion and new railway lines. And the fifth 
suggestion is, opportunity of employment in railway services should be 
given to properly qualified, deserving people from all States and Union 
Territories, following the principle of equality, so that they will get 
the chances. Sir, this Department of Railways has many new problems. Now, 
the incident that had taken place in Mumbai is an eye- opener. The 
terrorists had made Mumbai a target. The railway stations in big 
metropolitan cities have become rather unsafe. Therefore, a lot of money 
will have to be spent on security forces to protect the railway stations 
and the people there. So, these are some of the suggestions. 
Sir, I come from Maharashtra. There is a new railway line taken up by 
the Ministry, that is, Nagar- Beede-Parli. It is not more than 150  
kilometers. This line had been, approved in the year 1994. But the work 
has not taken any momentum at all. For one reason or the other, whatever 
provision is made lapses and, that is why, the work does not get any 
progress at all.

particular problem. In this interim Rail Budget, Mumbai should have been 
given some priority, because 80 per cent people daily travel in the city 
by local trains and they are in a shambles. Therefore, I would like to 
draw the attention of the Minister to this problem. Some more provision 
should be made for the local trains in Mumbai city itself. These are some 
of the suggestions. I would request the Railway Minister to think over 
that. Thank you very much for giving me this opportunity.

SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA (Assam): Thank you Sir. I am thankful to 
you for giving me this opportunity to speak on the Interim Railway Budget 
presented by the hon. Railway Minister, Shri Lalu Prasad Yadavji. Sir, in 
his Budget Speech, the Railway Minister has announced Rs. 10,807 crores 
as Estimated Budget for implementation of the Report of Sixth Pay 
Commission, which will benefit lakhs of workers and officials of Indian 
Railways and funding of various on-going Railway projects of our country. 
Sir, in his Budget Speech, the hon. Minister cat egorically said, proudly 
said that in the last five years Indian Railways' net profit is 
approximately Rs. 90,000 crores after decreasing the Railway fares, cost 
of Railway tickets in various classes of the Indian Railways. No doubt, 
this is a great achievement of the Indian Railways and we must 
congratulate the hon. Minister for his successful tenure. From the 
national point of view, although the Budget is a good Budget, but, it is 
very painful to say, Sir, that this Budget has totally neglected Assam 
and North-Eastern Region. This is a good Budget for other parts of the 
country. But, this is a bad Budget for the States like Assam and other 
North-Eastern States. I think, while preparing the Budget, the hon. 
Railway Minister might have forgotten Assam and the other North- Eastern 
region. But, Sir, Assam is a part of India. There is no doubt that only a 
few States are benefited from this Budget. Frankly speaking, due to this 
Budget, the regional imbalance among the States in our country is going 
to be increase. The Railway Ministry has totally failed to reduce 
regional imbalance in our country. 
Sir, in his Budget Speech, the hon. Minister has announced various 
schemes, including the dream project of Bullet Train. Sir, bullet train 
is the most sophisticated super fast train of the world. It is running in 
France, Germany, Japan, etc. No doubt, it is a good move as all the 
developed countries are using bullet train. I am ready to say that, on 
the one hand, the hon. Minister is introducing bullet train and on, the 
other  there are no electrical lines in many parts of the country, there 
are no broad gauge lines, and there are no lines in various parts of 
Assam and the North- Eastern Region. Why is this discrimination? We have 
nothing to say against the introduction of bullet train. But, in the 
meantime, the Government should seriously think that there should be 
electrical rail line in Assam. There are no electrical rail lines in 

432 
Assam. Can anybody imagine this? There is no broad gauge railway line. 
There is no railway line in many parts of the North- Eastern Region. I 
hope the hon. Minister take this very seriously. Sir, in his speech, the 
hon. Minister said, 'Indian Railway Ministry, in the coming years, is 
going to introduce 42 new trains in our country.' It is good. But, among 
these 42 new trains, not a single train is included for Assam or for any 
State of the North- Eastern Region! I hope I will get support from the 
House in this regard.  
Another important point, Sir, is, Assam is an insurgency- hit area. It 
is known to everybody. Unemployment is a big problem in our State. So, in 
the last Budget Session, when I took part in the general discussion on 
the Railway Budget, I categorically requested the hon. Minister to look 
after this region and announce job reservation for local youth of the 
North-Eastern Region and Assam. In his Budget speech, the hon. Railway 
Minister has proposed to recruit 22,000 additional personnel for  

433 
3.00 P.M. 
the Railway Protection Force and to create Battalions and Special 
Protection Force. So, I  would like to request the hon. Minister to 
protect the interests of the people of Assam and the people of the North-
East Region by announcing that there will be 100 per cent reservation for 
the local youth for the jobs in the North- Eastern Region. The Government 
should announce a policy in this regard. 
We also demand a coach factory in Assam. The Government is going to 
start a coach factory in Kerala. It is, no doubt, a very welcome step. 
But we-request that a coach factory should also be opened in Assam. It is 
a long-pending demand of the people of Assam. 
In the interest of the development of Assam and the North- East Region, 
we request that a separate railway zone should be opened in the North-
East Region. It should be a separate railway zone, excluding Bihar and 
Bengal. This railway zone in the North- East Region will, to some extent, 
also solve the unemployment problem of the Region. 
According to a health survey, the maximum number of cancer patients 
belong to Assam and the North-East Region. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Conclude please. 
SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA: Sir, please give me some more time 
because we have got nothing from the Railway Budget. I request you to 
give me just a few more minutes. So, Sir, I was saying that, "according 
to a health survey, the maximum number of cancer patients belong to Assam 
and the North- East Region. Every day, hundreds of cancer patients from 
Assam and from the North- East Region travel to Chennai and Mumbai for 
better medical treatment. But it is very difficult to travel to Chennai 
and Mumbai because there is only one train from Guwahati to Mumbai. It is 
also not a regular train. So, we would like to request the hon. Minister 
to introduce a super fast train from Dubrigarh to Chennai and from 
Dubrigarh to Mumbai. 
In the year 1997, the then Prime Minister had laid the foundation 
stone of the Bogibeel Bridge in Assam. In the last Winter Session of 
Parliament, in response to one of my questions, the hon. Railway Minister 
had informed us that the Bogibeel Bridge would be completed by the year 
2012. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: You have taken a lot of time, Mr. Baishya. 
SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA: But recently, the Railway officers told 

434 
us that it is going to be completed by 2015. Sir, frankly speaking, the 
progress in the construction of Bogibeel Bridge is very slow. It is so 
slow that out of 27 pillars, which are to be constructed there, not even 
a single pillar has been constructed till date. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Mr. Baishya, there are a number of speakers. I 
can't give indefinite time to you. So, please conclude now. 
SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA: Sir, I am concluding. Although the 
foundation stone for this bridge was laid in 1997, not a single pillar 
has been constructed as yet. This is due to lack of funds. When the 
Indian Railways is making a profit of more than Rs. 90,000/-  crores, and 
when it is going to  

435 
introduce the bullet train in the country, why is Assam not getting money 
for construction of a bridge? This is the sentiment of our people. I 
request the hon. Minister to understand our sentiment. Please try to 
understand the situation prevalent in Assam. 
I would request the hon. Railway Minister to develop the Guwahati 
Railway Station and to modernise it. This is the need of the hour. Sir, 
Guwahati is the hub of the North Eastern Region. There are seven sister 
States, namely, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, 
Nagaland and Tripura. And, Guwahati is the hub of the North Eastern 
Region. Being the hub of the North Eastern Region, it is the duty of the 
Government to modernise the Guwahati Railway Station. I hope he will look 
into these issues and will, definitely, fulfil our demands. Thank you.

SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA : Mr. Vice- Chairman, Sir, the Railways is a much 
sought after mode of travel for comfort and safety at a cheaper cost. It 
is a well- known fact. Sir, I take this opportunity to congratulate and 
appreciate the hon. Minister of Railways, Shri Lalu Prasad Yadav for 
having engineered the train of the Indian Railways to achieve record 
profits, maintaining, at the same time, the standard of service and 
efficiency, continuously for four years. Adoption of new technologies by 
the Railways has increased the safety and security of the passengers 
also. There may be one or to mishappenings, but at the same time, we 
should agree that comparatively, it is much less than it was in the past. 
I do not need to take much time of the House. It is a well- known and 
established fact that after Laluji assumed office of the Railways, it is 
all for appreciations from all quarters. I wanted to say this while 
summing up my speech. This time, I personally want to congratulate and 
thank him on behalf of my State, Tamil Nadu, for he has announced five 
new trains and has also introduced two- three extension trains and he has 
conceded all the demands of our leader, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, 
Dr. Kalaignar. Personally, Sir, when I spoke on the Railway Budget last 
time, I had demanded a daytime inter-city train from Trichy to 
Tirunelvelii. Thanks to the hon. Railway Minister and the Minister of 
State, Shri R. Velu, for taking the initiative and now they have 
announced introduction of a new train from Trichy to Madurai and Madurai 
to Trichy which will help all the people who go to the Madurai High 
Court. Personally, we are very grateful to them. When we speak something 
on the floor of the House during a debate, generally, it is being 
listened to. But he has accommodated the recommendations of the Members 
of Parliament. He has reciprocated and conceded many of our demands. Even 

464 
my colleagues said that the extension of the Chennai- Nagore train would 
be a boon to the Thiruvarur people, our leader's birthplace. 
Sir, I want to bring one or two demands, especially, to the notice of 
the Minister of State, Shri Veluji. We need a train from Mayiladuthuri to 
Coimbatore, and one daytime inter- city train from Trichy to Bangalore 
which will have a very good patronage and it will be well appreciated by 
all; so also a tri-weekly train from Madurai to Tirupathi, which has been 
suggested by many people from all quarters. Laluji may not be accessible 
to the last man, but his train is accessible to the last man. It serves  
every  ordinary  poor person. I am very happy that this UPA Government 
and also the President in her  

465 
Address has lauded to the higher most level, Laluji's performance in the 
Railways, especially, quoting the construction of a dedicated freight 
corridor between Kolkata and Ludhiana on the Eastern route and Mumbai and 
Dadri on the Western route to augment the capacity of carrying freight 
traffic. He has won accolades from the President to the last citizen. I 
thank him once again. Moreover, I have one important demand. He is very 
compassionate to the senior citizens and all the people, invariably. I 
think he would concede this demand also. I request him, on behalf of the 
old-age parents of the Railway employees, that they should be treated as 
dependents of the family unit so that they can become eligible for 
medical facilities and family free passes. This would not incur much 
expenses for the Railways. At present, there are 10 categories of the 
Railway Family Unit. I will just quote one thing which is quite strange. 
Taking the parents of the Railway employees into the'family unit would 
not cost the Railways much. In one category, it says: "...the sons of 
railway employees, over 21 years of age, without an upper age limit, even 
if not a student or invalid, provided he is wholly dependent on and 
resides with the railway employees." It goes on like that, and there you 
have ten categories. Here, as I mentioned, including the aged parents of 
the railway employees into the family unit will get you a very good name, 
and people will appreciate you, especially, in the present times, when 
people are let down by their children themselves. All these things will 
add feather to the cap of the UPA Government. 
I would like to say only one thing to the hon. Railway Minister. Some 
Members criticised you; some did not appreciate what you have done. And, 
there may be some demands which have not been fulfilled. I would like to 
quote a few lines from a Tamil poem: 
"Potruvar potrattum; puzhudhi vaari thootruvaar thootrattum. 
Etradhoru karuthu enadhullam enruraithaal, evar varinum nillane, 
anjane." 
It means, "Whoever wants to praise us, let them praise. Whoever wants 
to abuse us, let them abuse. If my mind says that it is right, then, I 
will march on. I won't be afraid of anybody. I won't stop for anybody 
because my goal is clear." That is the goal of Laluji, and that is the 
goal of the UPA. Thank you, Sir. 
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, as the Representative of 
Andhra Pradesh, I want to convey the sentiments of the people of Andhra 
Pradesh that they have got a very raw deal in the Railway Budget. Even 

466 
though a common proverb says, "कर  मेहनत तो खा नेमत, मेहनत का फल ´ÖßšüÖ", 
but, here, in spite  of the efficiency, in spite of the revenue increase 
by the South-Central Railway, we have not got that type of a deal which 
the people of Andhra Pradesh had expected. 
The hon. Member, Shri Girish Sanghi has given some suggestions and I 
fully endorse his view. Shatabdi Express should be introduced linking 
Hyderabad to various other important neighbouring cities. While coming to 
other problems, the Tatkal system, as many of my colleagues have also 
mentioned, should be rationalized properly. Presently, a person, starting 
his journey from Delhi, wanting to get down at Nagpur or Hyderabad, is 
charged up to Yeshwantpur, Bengaluru. I think this is irrational. So, it 
has to be rationalized properly. 

467 
As regards internet booking of tickets, I think, the city code should 
be simplified, as it is there in the U.S. and other countries. Most of 
the time, while searching for stations on the internet, it becomes very 
difficult. So, I feel that the Ministry should find a more simplified 
method. Then, I am sorry to say that there is not even a single toll free 
number for the Railways. I think it is the urgent need of the hour. 
Secondly, whenever any accident takes place, you divert the train from 
one place to another. But the time limit is not properly adhered to. In 
such a situation, there is a delay of seven or eight hours also. In this 
situation also, we have to adhere to the time table. Sir, what I would 
like to say is that even though the efficiency of the Railways has 
increased, yet, punctuality has become the casualty. For the past six 
months, I have travelled extensively to several places. Believe me, 
except at two or three places, 10 per cent of the trains reached at the 
correct time – 90 per cent of the trains reached their destinations late, 
ranging from 30 minutes to even eight hours. This is my personal 
experience. I do not know why Laluji is not in a position to make 
punctuality a strict code. That is my personal request. 
I have one more request to make on behalf of the people of Hyderabad. 
People, in great numbers, go to Ajmer Sharief Durgah. Just like we have 
the Kaifiat Express in the name of Kaifi Azmi, if a train in the name of 
Maqdoom Mohiuddin, who was also a very great poet of India, could be 
introduced from Kacheguda to Ajmer, either bi-weekly or tri-weekly, then, 
the people of Hyderabad would feel highly thankful. 
Then, as per the Catering Policy, 2005, where 12 per cent licence fee 
is to be charged on the annual sales turnover, the IRCTC, at the time of 
fixing the licence fee, is not adhering to the norms and code. 
Then, I just wanted to remind that the Standing Committee on Railways 
in its Report of 2006- 07 has said that snacks and light refreshment 
should be made available on no- profit-no-loss basis. The Standing 
Committee had also attacked the new policy of commercialisation and 
profiteering of this business. It had recommended that the Railways 
should not exploit the food and snack business by making it a profit-
making business and that the Railways should not leave its social 
obligation. Sir, this policy of commercialisation and profiteering has 
clearly endangered the livelihood of 24 lakh food vendors which will 
affect nearly 1.5 crore dependents who belong to the Dalits or 
minorities, women, OBCs and other categories. Even though Laluji had 
assured on the floor of Lok Sabha that he would protect the interests of 
the Dalits and STs from the purview of the IRCTC, but it is not being 
implemented. I just wanted to draw his attention this issue. 

468 
Finally, I have gone through the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor 
General for the year 2006- 07. They have pointed out so many serious 
lapses. If you look at this Report from Chapter 2 to 5, you will find a 
net loss of Rs. 1630.67 crores. The Railway Minister should look into 
this Report and try to rectify it so that profits can further be 
increased. 
Lastly, my colleague was just pointing out that Asansol is the 6th 
fastest growing city in India. The Railway Ministry should take this into 
consideration and see to it that Rajdhani stops at Asansol and it also 
gets connected to various other cities.

STATEMENT BY MINISTER – contd. 
National Ganga River Basin Authority 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI 
NAMO NARAIN MEENA): Sir, the need for revamping the Ganga cleaning 
programme has been widely recognised. Hitherto, the implementation has 
been piecemeal and focussed more on municipal sewage. The problem is 
compounded by inadequate flows. It was felt that a comprehensive response 
is necessary, covering water quality and flow, sustainable access, 
prevention and control of pollution, food and energy security, in the 
form of a national mission by giving the Ganga the status of a National 
River. Ganga has a special place in the hearts and minds of all Indians 
and this needs to be recognised. It was felt that a model for river 
cleaning should be set up through a new institutional mechanism. 
Accordingly, the Central Government has decided to give Ganga the 
status of a 'National Riverङ  and set up a 'National Ganga River Basin 
Authorityङ as an empowered planning, financing, monitoring and 
coordinating authority for the Ganga River under the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986. The Authority will be chaired by the Prime 
Minister and have as it members, the Chief Ministers of the concerned 
States. The Authority will be vested with appropriate powers to carry out 

500 
its functions. A notification in this regard is being issued by the 
Government. 
The National Ganga River Basin Authority would be responsible for 
addressing the problem of pollution in the Ganga in a holistic and 
comprehensive manner. This will include water quality, minimum ecological 
flows, sustainable access and other issues relevant to river ecology and 
management. Under the new approach, the river basin will be the unit of 
planning. 
The Authority would combine regulatory and developmental functions 
keeping in view powers  

501 
vested with the State Governments and its institutions. It is expected 
that this would rejuvenate the collective efforts of the Centre and the 
States for cleaning the river Ganga and help accomplish the mission that 
had been initiated in 1985 by the then Prime Minister Shri Rajiv Gandhi.
